### Discovery & Translational Science

* **[Big Pharma]** **Roche partners with Defand Therapeutics on molecular glues** [STAT+](https://www.statnews.com/2026/10/08/roche-defand-therapeutics-drug-development-deal/)
  * Roche has established a drug discovery collaboration with Chinese biotech Defand Therapeutics.
  * The partnership is focused on the development of molecular glue medicines targeting novel disease-relevant proteins.

* **Novel molecular glues target ALK resistance** [Nature Reviews Drug Discovery](https://www.nature.com/articles/d41573-026-00163-w) / [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42844417/)
  * Newly developed molecular glues show activity in overcoming resistance mutations in anaplastic lymphoma kinase (ALK).

* **Preclinical development of PARP1-selective inhibitor DSB1559 in TNBC** [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42843923/)
  * The PARP1-selective inhibitor DSB1559 demonstrated superior antitumor efficacy and stimulated antitumor immunity in preclinical models of triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC).

* **Interleukin-10 autoantibodies identified in inflammatory bowel disease** [NEJM](https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMc2609242?af=R&rss=currentIssue)
  * Research identifies the presence and potential mechanistic role of autoantibodies targeting interleukin-10 (IL-10) in patients with inflammatory bowel disease (IBD).

* **AI-driven mass spectrometry in metabolomics and lipidomics for drug discovery** [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42844781/)
  * A review details the application of artificial intelligence (AI) methodologies in mass spectrometry-based metabolomics and lipidomics to accelerate early-stage drug discovery and development.

* **Other Discovery & Translational Literature Highlights** [NEJM](https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMra2500695?af=R&rss=currentIssue) / [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42844630/) / [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42844619/) / [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42844361/) / [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42843834/) / [NEJM](https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMms2607020?af=R&rss=currentIssue)
  * *Breast Cancer*: A review of advances in the systemic treatment of breast cancer, emphasizing personalized medicine, tailored treatments for older women, and novel combinations.
  * *Cell Therapy*: Updates on chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T-cell and T-cell receptor (TCR) T-cell therapies for solid tumors from ASCO 2026.
  * *Multiple Myeloma*: A systematic review and network meta-analysis of T-cell-redirecting therapies in early relapsed multiple myeloma.
  * *Autoimmune Engagers*: A review of next-generation immune cell engagers for B-cell depletion in autoimmune indications.
  * *Antipsychotic Discovery*: A three-part historical review of antipsychotic discovery, detailing initial insights, dopaminergic diversification, and muscarinic mechanisms.
  * *Reproducibility*: A perspective on transitioning clinical and biomedical science from simple study repetition to corroboration.

### Early Trials — Phase I–II

* **Optogenetic therapy RST-001 restores partial visual function in retinitis pigmentosa** [NEJM](https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMoa2602215?af=R&rss=currentIssue) / [STAT+](https://www.statnews.com/2026/10/07/optogenetics-restores-some-vision-retinitis-pigmentosa/) / [NEJM Editorial](https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMe2610388?af=R&rss=currentIssue)
  * In a small clinical trial evaluating an optogenetic therapeutic approach for retinitis pigmentosa, approximately 50% of treated patients regained photosensitivity in their vision.
  * The trial demonstrates clinical proof-of-concept for optogenetics in restoring targeted visual pathways in patients with advanced retinal degeneration.

* **Locoregional autologous NK cell therapy combined with HAIC in hepatocellular carcinoma** [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42845031/)
  * A Phase IIa trial evaluated high-dose autologous natural killer (NK) cell therapy administered locoregionally in combination with hepatic arterial infusion chemotherapy (HAIC) for locally advanced hepatocellular carcinoma.

* **Agomelatine improves symptoms in diarrhea-predominant irritable bowel syndrome** [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42844310/)
  * A randomized controlled clinical trial demonstrated that agomelatine significantly improved symptom severity and quality of life in patients with diarrhea-predominant irritable bowel syndrome (IBS-D).

* **Lemborexant improves daytime sleep in shift workers** [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42844407/)
  * A randomized, placebo-controlled trial showed that treatment with the dual orexin receptor antagonist lemborexant improved total daytime sleep duration in shift workers.

### Late & Pivotal Trials — Phase III

* **[Big Pharma]** **Upadacitinib shows sustained 5-year efficacy in psoriatic arthritis** [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42844553/)
  * Long-term safety and efficacy data from the Phase 3 SELECT-PsA 1 study showed sustained clinical benefits for upadacitinib (Rinvoq) over 5 years of treatment in patients with active psoriatic arthritis.

* **[Biotech]** **Enliven Therapeutics prepares Phase III trial for CML candidate relcobatinib** [BioPharma Dive](https://www.biopharmadive.com/news/halozyme-merck-europe-enliven-insmed-rougetx-kymathera/832282/)
  * Enliven has reached agreement with the FDA on the design of a pivotal, late-stage study evaluating its BCR-ABL1 inhibitor relcobatinib in chronic myeloid leukemia (CML).
  * The trial is planned to enroll 450 patients, positioning the drug as a direct competitor to Novartis’ asciminib (Scemblix) and Merck’s recently acquired Terns Pharmaceuticals assets.

* **Inhaled treprostinil clinical trial data in idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis** [NEJM](https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMc2610744?af=R&rss=currentIssue)
  * NEJM correspondence analyzes recent efficacy and clinical outcomes of inhaled treprostinil in patients with idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF).

### Regulatory & Approvals

* **[Big Pharma]** **FDA approves Pfizer's Tukysa in combination with trastuzumab and pertuzumab for HER2-positive breast cancer** [FDA](http://www.fda.gov/drugs/resources-information-approved-drugs/fda-approves-tucatinib-trastuzumab-and-pertuzumab-maintenance-treatment-her2-positive-breast-cancer)
  * The FDA approved tucatinib (Tukysa) in combination with trastuzumab and pertuzumab for the maintenance treatment of adults with unresectable locally advanced or metastatic HER2-positive breast cancer who showed no progression after 4–8 induction cycles.
  * The approval was based on the HER2CLIMB-05 trial (NCT05132582) of 654 patients, which met its primary endpoint of investigator-assessed progression-free survival (PFS).

* **[Biotech]** **Scholar Rock resubmits apitegromab MAA for Spinal Muscular Atrophy** [X/BioStocks](https://x.com/BioStocks/status/2108167103090180189)
  * Scholar Rock has resubmitted its Marketing Authorization Application (MAA) to the EMA for apitegromab, a selective inhibitor of myostatin activation, for the treatment of children and adults with spinal muscular atrophy (SMA).

* **[Biotech]** **Vir Biotechnology receives FDA Fast Track for prostate cancer candidate VIR-5500** [X/BioStocks](https://x.com/BioStocks/status/2108175190006042684)
  * The FDA has granted Fast Track designation to VIR-5500, an experimental therapy for the treatment of patients with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (mCRPC).

* **[Biotech]** **CATX receives FDA Fast Track for PSV359 in solitary fibrous tumors** [X/BioStocks](https://x.com/BioStocks/status/2108139697012723981)
  * PSV359 has been granted FDA Fast Track designation for the treatment of adult patients with locally advanced unresectable and/or metastatic fibroblast activation protein (FAP)-positive solitary fibrous tumors.

* **FDA Regulatory Updates and Guidances** [FDA Guidance](http://www.fda.gov/regulatory-information/search-fda-guidance-documents/pharmacokinetics-patients-impaired-hepatic-function-study-design-data-analysis-and-impact-dosing) / [FDA Guidances](http://www.fda.gov/vaccines-blood-biologics/biologics-guidances/recently-issued-guidance-documents) / [FDA News](http://www.fda.gov/drugs/news-events-human-drugs/whats-new-related-drugs)
  * *Hepatic Impairment Draft Guidance*: Issued draft guidance regarding pharmacokinetics in patients with impaired hepatic function, outlining study design, data analysis, and dosing recommendations.
  * *Biologics & CGT*: Released multiple guidances including CBER FAQs on developing cellular and gene therapy products, potency assessment of active immunotherapies, and container closure considerations for biosimilars.
  * *Kybella Labeling*: FDA issued a Drug Safety Communication adding warning information regarding adverse reactions to the labeling of Kybella (deoxycholic acid).

### Business & Strategy

* **[Big Pharma]** **Halozyme wins European patent injunction halting Merck's subcutaneous Keytruda** [STAT+](https://www.statnews.com/pharmalot/2026/10/07/merck-suffers-setback-in-europe-over-new-keytruda-formulation/) / [BioPharma Dive](https://www.biopharmadive.com/news/halozyme-merck-europe-enliven-insmed-rougetx-kymathera/832282/)
  * A Netherlands court has ordered a halt to the manufacturing and marketing of Merck’s subcutaneous formulation of pembrolizumab (Keytruda Qlex) in eight European countries.
  * The court ruled that Merck’s subcutaneous formulation infringed on Halozyme's patents covering technology designed to deliver large biologics via under-the-skin injection.
  * Halozyme has also won a similar legal proceeding in Germany and is actively challenging Merck in U.S. court. Competitors Bristol Myers Squibb and Roche have licensed Halozyme's technology for their respective subcutaneous products (Opdivo and Tecentriq).

* **[Biotech]** **Caribou Biosciences to halt CAR-T programs, lay off staff, and seek strategic alternatives** [BioPharma Dive](https://www.biopharmadive.com/news/caribou-layoffs-strategic-alternatives-allogeneic-cell-therapy-vispacel/832343/)
  * Pioneering CRISPR gene-editing developer Caribou Biosciences is discontinuing research, laying off a substantial portion of its workforce by year-end, and seeking strategic alternatives due to a difficult financing environment.
  * The decision halts development on two "off-the-shelf" allogeneic CAR-T cancer therapies, including one asset that was positioned to enter Phase 3 testing.
  * The board is exploring potential M&A options or asset divestments, reflecting industry-wide challenges with the long-term durability and financing of allogeneic therapies.

* **[Biotech]** **Biohaven enters $80M licensing deal with Ono Pharmaceutical** [X/BioStocks](https://x.com/BioStocks/status/2108135051250499797)
  * Biohaven has signed an exclusive licensing agreement with Japan's Ono Pharmaceutical to develop and commercialize its extracellular IgG degraders in Japan and select Asian territories.
  * Biohaven will receive an upfront payment of $80 million as part of the agreement.

* **[Biotech]** **Forbion raises record $2.6B venture capital fund** [STAT+](https://www.statnews.com/2026/10/07/biotech-news-forbion-raises-2-6-billion-largest-fundraise/)
  * European life sciences venture capital firm Forbion has raised $2.6 billion across its latest funds, marking the firm's largest fundraise to date and one of the largest regional pools of capital raised recently.

* **[Big Pharma]** **Eli Lilly outlines "multiple shots on goal" target strategy** [X/Jacob Plieth](https://x.com/JacobPlieth/status/2108122146043994535) / [X/Brad Loncar](https://x.com/bradloncar/status/2107856316618207504)
  * CEO Dave Ricks discussed a conscious strategy of advancing multiple candidates against single validated targets, pointing to candidates LY4052031 and LY4101174 targeting Nectin-4, and tersolisib, LY3849524, and LY4045004 targeting PI3Kα.
  * Ricks also detailed the company’s business development outlook, GLP-1 expansion plans, and Alzheimer's pipeline strategy.

* **[Biotech]** **Avidity Biosciences raises $50M through PIPE** [X/BioStocks](https://x.com/BioStocks/status/2108143692787966015)
  * Avidity Biosciences (RNA) secured a $50 million Private Investment in Public Equity (PIPE) financing, pricing shares at $7.93.

* **Evaluating clinical trial prediction markets as information sources** [NEJM](https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMp2610547?af=R&rss=currentIssue)
  * A perspective article analyzes the utility, information quality, and potential costs associated with prediction markets tracking clinical trial readouts.

### Public Health & Policy

* **PhRMA sues Trump administration over international reference pricing model** [STAT+](https://www.statnews.com/2026/10/07/phrma-sues-over-drug-pricing-model-globe/) / [STAT+ Pharmalittle](https://www.statnews.com/pharmalot/2026/10/08/phrma-suing-trump-biotech-frustration-tariffs-pharmalittle-newsletter/?utm_campaign=rss)
  * PhRMA, the primary trade group representing brand-name drug manufacturers, has filed a lawsuit against the Trump administration.
  * The legal challenge targets a pilot program that mandates lower Medicare drug prices by indexing them to drug prices in peer foreign countries.

* **Biotech firms face challenges securing exemptions from new import tariffs** [STAT+](https://www.statnews.com/2026/10/08/trump-tariffs-section-232-imported-prescription-drugs-challenge-biotech-companies/)
  * Small- and mid-sized biotechnology companies report difficulties navigating the application processes required to obtain exemptions from new Section 232 import taxes on active pharmaceutical ingredients (APIs) and raw materials.

* **Maternal and infant healthcare research and guidelines** [NEJM](https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMe2609170?af=R&rss=currentIssue) / [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42844453/)
  * *Sepsis Management*: An NEJM editorial reviews therapeutic diversity in managing pediatric and maternal septic shock.
  * *Pediatric Pneumonia*: A systematic review and meta-analysis of clinical trials comparing short-course versus long-course antibiotic therapies for non-severe community-acquired pneumonia (CAP) in children.

* **HHS leader proposes reforms to the CMS 340B drug discount program** [STAT+ Opinion](https://www.statnews.com/2026/10/08/340b-drug-discount-program-cms-reform-proposal/)
  * An HHS official argues that the 340B drug discount program has drifted from its original safety-net intent into an institutional subsidy for hospitals, outlining CMS proposals to reform the program's oversight.

* **Trump administration proposes $70k fee on international student work program** [STAT+](https://www.statnews.com/2026/10/07/trump-administration-proposes-fee-targeting-interational-students-optional-practical-training/)
  * The administration has proposed a $70,000 fee for the Optional Practical Training (OPT) work authorization program, a move that could significantly limit international STEM talent pipelines for U.S. academic and biotech R&D laboratories.

* **Gender representation among Nobel laureates remains heavily skewed** [STAT+](https://www.statnews.com/2026/10/08/health-news-nobel-boys-club-again-2026-winners/)
  * Analysis of the 2026 Nobel Prizes in physiology or medicine, physics, and chemistry shows that all six laureates selected this year were men; women make up only 4% of science laureates historically.

***

**Worth watching:** The escalating legal and commercial battle between Halozyme and Merck over subcutaneous Keytruda. With European courts already granting injunctions, the outcome of the pending U.S. patent lawsuit could significantly alter life-cycle management and royalty economics for the world's top-selling cancer immunotherapy.

- Biology & Health
    - [Bombshell Study Upends Low Carb Nutrition Science!](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=MXhnHpAx6YQ) -- Physionic
        - Cites research (Study 518) demonstrating that ketogenesis mitigates metabolic dysfunction–associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) via mechanisms that go beyond simple fat oxidation.
        - References clinical trials comparing ketogenic and non-ketogenic weight-loss diets to evaluate their distinct impacts on hepatic steatosis and mitochondrial metabolism in MASLD.
        - Compares the metabolic effects of short-term eucaloric low- and high-carbohydrate diets on liver triacylglycerol content in overweight and obese males, alongside studies on how macronutrient distribution affects insulin sensitivity during caloric restriction.
    - [A Great Company Can Still Be a Bad Investment](https://www.youtube.com/shorts/0FqqMf-0C10) -- Digital Health Inside Out
        - Patrick E. Donohue discusses the distinction between a company's operational strength and its viability as an investment.
        - Explains that Oura’s strength as a business does not automatically make it an attractive or high-performing investment opportunity.
        - Highlights that finding a business that simultaneously excels as a great company and a great investment is exceptionally rare in venture capital and health technology.
    - [Oura’s Real Edge Isn’t the Ring](https://www.youtube.com/shorts/t283NnCYGuA) -- Digital Health Inside Out
        - Patrick E. Donohue argues that wearable hardware in the healthtech space will eventually become a commoditized market.
        - Asserts that Oura's actual competitive advantage does not stem from its physical ring hardware.
        - States that Oura's long-term edge relies on how the company differentiates, utilizes, and monetizes its collected health data.
- Pure Science
    - [08 - Stinky  #mathctober](https://www.youtube.com/shorts/xtCPijKs_78) -- El Jj
        - Warnings are given that the video's mathematical content will quickly become outdated due to rapid, large-scale releases of new results by AI companies like OpenAI and Anthropic.
        - Mentions the potential for AI models to solve the remaining Millennium Prize Problems in mathematics.
        - The video is directly inspired by David Madore's 2026 article analyzing the concept of "AI and math destruction."
